title: United States of America
description: The United States is a federal republic of 50 states founded on the 1776 Declaration of Independence and the 1789 Constitution, with a presidential system and separation of powers. It spans North America from the Atlantic to the Pacific with about 340 million people, and its economy is the world's largest by nominal GDP. Its culture — film, music, technology, higher education — has global reach, and English is the dominant language with Spanish widely spoken.

print('founded 1776 (independence) / 1789 (constitution)')

title: People's Republic of China
description: China is the world's most populous country outside India, with about 1.4 billion people, governed as a one-party socialist state since 1949 with Beijing as capital. Its civilization spans millennia — paper, printing, gunpowder, the compass — and its modern economy is the world's second largest, built on manufacturing and increasingly technology. Mandarin is the official language, written in simplified characters.

title: Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (1922-1991)
description: The USSR was a federal socialist state spanning Eurasia from 1922 until its dissolution in December 1991, when its 15 republics became independent nations. It industrialized rapidly, launched the first satellite (Sputnik, 1957) and first human (Yuri Gagarin, 1961) into space, and was a Cold War superpower. Its planned economy, Russian-dominated administration, and one-party rule defined its government; its breakup redrew the map of Europe and Asia.

print('USSR: 1922-1991, 15 republics -> 15 independent nations')
print('Sputnik 1957, Gagarin 1961; dissolved December 1991')
provenance: Public reference: standard historical records and encyclopedic public sources; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia (1945-1992)
description: Yugoslavia was a Balkan federation of six republics (Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Serbia, Montenegro, Macedonia) that existed from 1945 until breaking apart in 1991-1992. Under Josip Broz Tito it pursued non-aligned socialism independent of Moscow. Its dissolution produced a series of wars in the 1990s and seven successor states, with Kosovo's status still disputed.

title: Kingdom of Prussia (1701-1918)
description: Prussia was a German kingdom from 1701 (a duchy and electorate before that) until the 1918 revolution, famed for military discipline, efficient bureaucracy, and leaders like Frederick the Great. It unified Germany around itself in 1871 as the German Empire's dominant state. After World War II the Allies formally dissolved Prussia in 1947; its lands are now in Germany, Poland, and Russia.

title: Roman Empire (27 BCE - 1453 CE)
description: The Roman Empire began with Augustus in 27 BCE, ruling the Mediterranean world at its height under Trajan (117 CE) from Britain to Egypt. It gave the West Latin, Roman law, engineering (roads, aqueducts), and Christianity's institutional spread. The western half fell in 476 CE; the eastern (Byzantine) half endured until Constantinople fell in 1453. Its legal and linguistic legacy underpins much of Europe and the Americas.

title: Ottoman Empire (c. 1299-1922)
description: The Ottoman Empire was a Turkish-Islamic empire spanning southeastern Europe, western Asia, and North Africa at its 16th-17th century height under sultans like Suleiman the Magnificent. It took Constantinople in 1453, ending the Byzantine Empire, and ruled a multi-ethnic, multi-religious state through the millet system. Defeat in World War I ended it; Mustafa Kemal Atatürk founded the Republic of Turkey from its Anatolian core in 1923.

title: Austro-Hungarian Empire (1867-1918)
description: Austria-Hungary was a dual monarchy created by the 1867 Compromise, joining the Austrian Empire and Kingdom of Hungary under one Habsburg ruler while keeping separate parliaments. It held a dozen nationalities together until World War I, which began with the assassination of its heir Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo (1914). Defeat dissolved it into Austria, Hungary, Czechoslovakia, and Yugoslav lands.

print('WWI trigger: Sarajevo 1914 -> dissolved into successor states')
provenance: Public reference: standard historical records and encyclopedic public sources; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Czechoslovakia (1918-1993)
description: Czechoslovakia was a Central European state of Czechs and Slovaks founded in 1918 from Austria-Hungary's breakup, dismembered by Nazi Germany in 1938-39, restored in 1945, communist from 1948, and peacefully split into the Czech Republic and Slovakia on January 1, 1993 — the 'Velvet Divorce.' Its interwar democracy and the 1968 Prague Spring are its defining historical moments.

title: Gran Colombia (1819-1831)
description: Gran Colombia was Simón Bolívar's republic uniting Venezuela, Colombia (then New Granada), Ecuador, and Panama from 1819 to 1831, forged in the wars of independence against Spain. Political rivalry between centralists and federalists — and Bolívar's failing health — broke it into Venezuela, Ecuador, and New Granada. Its flag's yellow-blue-red tricolor survives in all three successor states.

title: Republic of Texas (1836-1845)
description: The Republic of Texas was an independent nation from 1836 (after San Jacinto ended Mexican rule) until U.S. annexation in 1845, with Sam Houston as its best-known president. It issued its own currency, maintained diplomatic relations with several European powers, and carried a large public debt. Annexation led directly to the Mexican-American War (1846-1848).

title: Byzantine Empire (330-1453)
description: The Byzantine Empire was the eastern Roman Empire centered on Constantinople, enduring from Constantine's founding (330 CE) to the Ottoman conquest (1453). It preserved Roman law (Justinian's Code), Greek learning, and Orthodox Christianity, and its diplomacy, bureaucracy, and military manuals influenced medieval Europe and Russia. Its thousand-year run makes it one of history's longest-lived states.

title: Mongol Empire (1206-1368)
description: The Mongol Empire, founded by Genghis Khan in 1206, became the largest contiguous land empire in history, stretching from Eastern Europe to the Pacific. Its Pax Mongolica reopened the Silk Road, spread technologies (including gunpowder westward), and practiced striking religious tolerance for a conquest state. It fragmented into khanates — Yuan China, the Golden Horde, the Ilkhanate, the Chagatai — within generations.

print('Mongol Empire 1206-1368: largest contiguous land empire ever')
print('Pax Mongolica: Silk Road, tech diffusion, religious tolerance')

title: Kingdom of Hawaii (1795-1893)
description: The Kingdom of Hawaii was a unified independent monarchy from Kamehameha I's conquest (1795, consolidated 1810) until American business interests overthrew Queen Lili'uokalani in 1893. It had a written constitution (1840), universal male suffrage unusually early, and diplomatic recognition from major powers. Annexation by the U.S. followed in 1898; it became the 50th state in 1959.

title: Empire of Brazil (1822-1889)
description: The Empire of Brazil was a constitutional monarchy under Pedro I and Pedro II from independence (1822) until a military coup proclaimed the republic in 1889. It abolished slavery in 1888 (the last Western country to do so), built railways and a national bureaucracy, and kept Brazil's continental unity where Spanish America fragmented. Its green-and-yellow flag colors survive in the republican flag.
